take_homes: You can't hand over an agent. Context, boundary and checks copy, but someone has to answer for it, and I haven't named that person for anything I've built.
Ask what the teammate does today and what would have to be true for them to drop it, before I build anything for them.
Giving access and people using it are two different things. Deciders who didn't do the work don't act on the result, so involve them early.

monday.move: Message the head of sales and ask for twenty minutes. Ask how they prep for customer calls today, and don't mention the agent. Only after that decide whether to build anything.
monday.when: Monday morning, before I open Claude Code
monday.stop_condition: They're fine with what they do now, or they say nobody on their side would own a tool. Then I don't build the sales setup.
monday.blocker: I'll want to build it over the weekend first. Nobody outside engineering has asked for it, and I still don't know who would maintain it.

misconception.why: The module was about adoption and who owns it, not about checking output. I skipped the review steps and nothing slowed me down there. The only thing that did was the empty people plan.

one_line: Skip the infra talk. The useful part is that you can copy an agent's context but not who answers for it, and that you should ask the person first.
